Details RFx ID : 35058803 Tender Name : Con 27-01 - Three Waters Services Contract – Treatment Facilities Operations and Maintenance Reference # : Con 27-01 Open Date : Thursday, 1 October 2026 12:00 PM (Pacific/Auckland UTC+13:00) Close Date : Thursday, 19 November 2026 2:00 PM (Pacific/Auckland UTC+13:00) Tender Type : Request for Proposals (RFP) Tender Coverage : Sole Agency [?] Categories : 83000000 - Public Utilities and Public Sector Related Services Regions: New Zealand Exemption Reason : None Required Pre-qualifications : None Contact : Geoff Gray 0800 732 732 Alternate Physical Delivery Address : Alternate Physical Fax Number : Overview Southland District Council (SDC / Council /the Principal) maintains ownership and responsibility for managing the water services activity, comprising water, wastewater and stormwater, and undertaking the necessary planning and works to meet the levels of service for its community. In order to increase oversight and visibility of the water services, Council has adopted an in-house business unit with increasing in-house capability and capacity and will be delivering the water services under a number of separate contracts. Council will be delivering the water services under separate contracts from 1 July 2027. This Contract relates specifically to the operations and maintenance of Council’s treatment facilities including raw water intakes, water and wastewater treatment plants, pump stations and reservoirs / storage tanks. A high level of collaboration is expected between this Contract and those for reticulation, mechanical and electrical and SCADA / automation operations and maintenance. The specifications under this Contract are aimed at delivering an outcome focussed approach that enables SDC to meet their collective vision and levels of service for water, wastewater and stormwater activities. To support cost-effective delivery across multiple contracts, Council is seeking a collaborative approach, building successful relationships specifically for this Contract as well as with the other contractors delivering the water services. The overarching philosophy is to balance the work programmes against service levels within Council’s budget expectations, delivering a pro-active best-for-network approach. By working together, the reactive and routine maintenance and renewals can be optimised to reduce the overall costs and risks without compromising public safety, legislative requirements or service levels for the Southland community. Note: Please submit on the locked version of the schedules - documents located at: https://southlanddistrictcouncil.sharefile.com/public/share/web-s3b96309b847f4df This is a two-envelope procurement process. Proposals are to be submitted electronically in two separate electronic files via GETS. File 1 – “NON-PRICE SUBMISSION” NAME OF THE RESPONDENT shall not contain any information regarding price. If price information is included, the Principal may treat the Proposal as being invalid. File 2 – “PRICE SUBMISSION” NAME OF THE RESPONDENT shall contain the price information, including any price-related assumptions. The supplier(s) will provide technical advice, international development expertise, and stakeholder engagement support to help inform renewable energy investments and initiatives across Indonesia, Africa, and the Caribbean. This support will ensure activities are strategically targeted, responsive to partner-country needs, and contribute to increased access to sustainable renewable energy solutions. Services will include technical advice and support across MFAT’s existing renewable energy activities. This procurement represents a continuation of the current technical advisory services model rather than the introduction of a new approach. The estimated whole-of-life value is up to NZD $800,000 across all contracts. This procurement may result in up to three separate contracts. MFAT intends to use a single-stage Request for Proposal (RFP) with pre-conditions. To be eligible, respondents will need to demonstrate: • Relevant renewable energy and geothermal advisory experience • Relevant international development experience • No unmanaged conflicts of interest The evaluation methodology will be detailed in the RFP and is expected to involve a two-stage process. Eligible written proposals will be assessed against the evaluation criteria to determine a shortlist. Shortlisted respondents may then be invited to participate in an interview or clarification session before a final evaluation outcome is determined. Respondents (or consortium leads) must demonstrate the capability, experience, and expertise required to successfully deliver the intended outcomes. Further details on scope, requirements, and evaluation criteria will be provided in the RFP. This is an advance notice only and is not a tender process. MFAT expects to release the RFP in mid-to-late November 2026, with services anticipated to commence in early 2027. Recognising the Christmas and New Year period, the RFP will remain open into the new year to provide respondents sufficient time to prepare submissions. Interested suppliers should subscribe to this notice on GETS. An online supplier briefing is expected following release of the RFP. Boffa Miskell, in conjunction with Marlborough District Council, is providing advance notice of an upcoming procurement opportunity for helicopter operators to support wilding conifer control works within the Branch / Leatham and Waihopai management units. The opportunity will be undertaken through a two-stage procurement process. The first stage will invite helicopter operators who have an operating base in the Nelson/Tasman or Marlborough regions to apply for appointment to the Boffa Miskell Biosecurity Supplier Panel. Operators successfully appointed to the Panel will then be invited to participate in a closed competitive tender for the Branch / Leatham and Waihopai wilding conifer control works for a one-year period. This opportunity is part of New Zealand’s International Development Cooperation (IDC) Programme, and is targeting main contractors for the provision of ECI services for the Niue Justice Building. This opportunity may lead to continuation to Construction services. MFAT is working in partnership with the Government of Niue to design and construct a new Justice Building to enable effective, reliable and inclusive justice services. The new facility will incorporate courtrooms, judicial chambers, office space, a court registry and archival space. MFAT anticipates entering into an ECI pre-construction services contract with the selected supplier. Continuation of ECI to delivery of Construction services via NZS3910:2023 will be subject to a number of criteria, including funding approvals, supplier performance, successful achievement of ECI deliverables and progress through pre-agreed milestones, including achieving mutually agreeable contract terms and pricing reviews. The procurement will be conducted via an open market, two-stage tender process. This ROI phase will be used to create a shortlist who will then be invited to submit a response to a closed Request for Proposal. MFAT is looking to appoint an ECI supplier in mid-2027. The supplier will be expected to work collaboratively with MFAT, Government of Niue and consulting team/s. This opportunity may lead to continuation to construction services. If you are interested in this opportunity, please subscribe to this GETs notice and review the attached documentation. The ROI document sets out further details of the project and anticipated timetable. The ROI evaluation includes pre-conditions relevant to the project, and will consider capability and capacity and Respondents’ track record. Please also note the ROI Terms and Conditions.
